title: Evidence-led model risk and opportunity dossier for enterprise procurement
creator: Sophie Martinez
description: Purpose: Produce a compact, evidence-driven dossier to guide enterprise procurement decisions when selecting or approving LLM models for regulated customers. Scope: top 40 open and commercial models by production relevance (latency/cost/enterprise-compatibility), with both quantitative metrics and qualitative vendor/regulatory posture notes. Deliverables: a scored model catalog (CSV + Confluence), a one-page executive risk/opportunity summary, and recommended procurement guardrails (SLA, KMS, data residency, fallback policy).
scoring_framework: Primary axes: 1) Latency economics (30%) — measured by p50/p95 per-token cost at typical shard sizes; 2) Reliability & compatibility (25%) — availability of quantized variants, kernel maturity, memory profile; 3) Security & compliance posture (20%) — KMS/HSM support, license risk, known data-usage clauses; 4) Quality on enterprise prompts (15%) — closed-set evals and adversarial prompts; 5) Vendor/Community velocity (10%) — cadence of releases, security fixes. Scores normalized 0-100 and combined weighted to an overall procurement-fit score.
methodology: We run controlled runtime experiments on representative payload mixes (short chat, long context summaries, embeddings) across smallest-to-largest recommended sequence lengths. Combine telemetry with license/legal scans and vendor self-reported guarantees. Each model gets a confidence band based on sample size and known variance; models with low sample coverage flagged for follow-up POVs. Manual review performed by Research + Legal for top 12 candidates.

decisions: Use weighted scoring framework (latency economics + reliability + security + quality + velocity) as single procurement-fit metric.
Prioritize models with existing quantized kernels AND published memory profiles for enterprise pilot.
Flag models with license restrictions as 'requires legal approval' — do not recommend for automatic procurement without contract review.
tradeoffs_and_notes: Aggressive weighting toward latency economics improves cost predictability but can bias against newer high-quality models that lack optimized kernels.
We accept a small number of low-confidence scores to surface early-stage model opportunities — they require explicit POV experiments before procurement approval.
Observed correlation between vendor velocity and reduced security lag, but correlation is noisy for community models; recommend continuous monitoring rather than one-time approval.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible CSV with per-model metrics (latency p50/p95, cost estimator, memory footprint) for at least 30 representative workloads.
Confluence dossier with scored catalog and executive one-pager summarizing top 5 recommended models and top 3 'do-not-procure' flags.
Sign-off from Legal and Research on top 12 models; documented mitigation plans for any flagged license/regulatory issues.
Handoff ticket to Sales Ops that encodes procurement guardrails (SLA minimums, KMS requirements, allowed regions).
